Subject: Integration tooling matrix & error strategy — OptiCore POC

Hi Julia / Markus,

Great to meet yesterday — thanks for carving out time. Quick recap + recommended next steps from our side so you have something actionable to share with your engineers:

Summary of ask (from call)
- Real-time invoice extraction + routing to payments system (low latency for user-facing flows)
- Batch cleanup and classification for legacy records (higher throughput, can tolerate more latency)
- Auditability + retention requirements (SOC2, customer data scoping)

High-level integration approach
1) SDK + auth: use Redwood client SDK in your Services layer (node/java). Service-to-Redwood auth via short-lived JWTs minted by your Auth service (examples attached in auth-snippets.md).
2) Tool/function definitions: expose 2 functions to the model — "fetchCustomerProfile" (sync REST), and "submitPaymentProposal" (idempotent POST). See fn-definitions.jsonl for suggested function signatures and example structured outputs.
3) Embeddings + rerank: use embeddings for semantic search over historic invoices, then a lightweight reranker (250–500 tokens) for final selection. We recommend an embed model for batch index creation and a low-latency cross-encoder as reranker for user flows.
4) Parallel tool execution: optimistic parallel calls to non-conflicting read-only adapters (inventory price checks, FX rates) and sequential execution for stateful write ops. Fail open for read-only; strict rollback for write failures.
5) Error handling: structured error types returned to the model (e.g., {code: RATE_LIMIT, retry_after: 120}), plus client-side orchestration with idempotency tokens.

Attachments: integration-matrix.xlsx (proposed matrix of adapters + latency/cost tiers), auth-snippets.md (JWT minting examples), fn-definitions.jsonl (function schema examples).

Requested next steps
- Julia: confirm which adapters are read-only vs stateful (FX, customer-profile reads, payments writes) — one-liner suffices.
- OptiCore eng: share any existing idempotency / correlation id patterns you want preserved.
- We: schedule a 45-min technical pairing session next week to walk the SDK auth flow and function wiring.

If it helps, I can drop a minimal sample repo that wires the SDK + one stub adapter before the call.

Thanks,
Ben

Thanks Ben — useful summary. A few clarifying questions from our infra team so we can prep for the pairing session: 

1) Auth: for the short-lived JWT approach — can the SDK accept a delegated token minted by our external IdP (Azure AD)? If so, do you expect an intermediate Redwood token exchange or will you accept our token directly?

2) Parallel tools: we have an FX service that both reads rates and writes FX hedges (separate endpoints). For the optimistic parallel pattern, do you recommend splitting the adapter into two logical tools (fx_read, fx_write) or one tool with a mode flag?

3) Reranker: curious about throughput — in user-facing flows (peak 400 rps) what instance sizing do you recommend and is there a preferred quantized model for reranking to cut costs?

4) Error surface: do you have a recommended mapping between Redwood API error codes and our HTTP 4xx/5xx responses so our platform engineers can wire retries correctly?

We can confirm read vs stateful by EOD tomorrow. Also — happy to take the pairing session on Tue 10–11am CET if that works for your team.

Julia — great questions, answered inline below. I've also attached a short mapping file in auth-snippets.md and a sample error-mapping table in the matrix workbook.

1) Auth
- We can accept Azure AD tokens but recommend a short-lived Redwood session token for fine-grained scoping and rotation. Typical flow: your backend mints a signed assertion -> Redwood token exchange endpoint -> Redwood returns short-lived session token the SDK uses. This avoids exposing long-lived external tokens to client-side code. See auth-snippets.md for the exchange curl.

2) Parallel tools for FX service
- Prefer splitting into logical tools: fx_read (idempotent readonly) and fx_write (stateful). Keeps function signatures small and makes sandboxing easier (we can apply different timeout/retry policies per tool).

3) Reranker sizing and model choice
- For 400 rps user flows: we recommend a dedicated low-latency reranker pool (quantized 8-bit model on T4/RTX-class instances). Start with 2x 8-GPU pods behind autoscaler (target 20–30ms p95 per call) and tune. If budget-constrained, consider an on-demand cross-encoder with caching for hot queries.

4) Error mapping
- Recommended mapping (high level):
  - Redwood RATE_LIMIT -> http 429 (include Retry-After)
  - Redwood INVALID_INPUT -> http 400 (no retry)
  - Redwood DEPENDENCY_FAILURE -> http 502/503 (retry with backoff)
  - Redwood UNAUTHORIZED -> http 401 (re-auth)

Proposed pairing session: Tue 23 Mar 2027 10:00–10:45 CET (we'll send a calendar invite). We'll bring a tiny sample repo that:
- wires SDK auth exchange (short-lived token)
- shows function definitions wired to mock fx_read/fx_write adapters
- demonstrates parallel read-only tool fanout with fail-open behavior

Action items captured:

Thanks,
Ben

Looping in a couple of architectural notes from the infra playbook that I think will be useful during pairing:

- Tool definitions: prefer small deterministic signatures. Example (pseudo):
  fn fetchCustomerProfile(customer_id: string) -> {status, profile: {name, tier, kyc}}
  fn submitPaymentProposal(tx_id: string, amount: int, idempotency_key: string) -> {status, confirmation_id?}

- Parallel execution pattern:
  - Fanout reads in parallel (fx_read, inventory_read), collect results, then run reranker/synth step to pick candidate.
  - Serialize writes: run submitPaymentProposal only after candidate chosen.
  - For optimistic parallel patterns, attach correlation_id so writes can be reconciled if the read results were slightly stale.

- Error handling: standardized structured errors (type, code, retryable, retry_after). Client orchestration should:
  1) Retry transient errors with exponential backoff (bounded to 3 attempts),
  2) For RATE_LIMIT include jitter + respect retry_after,
  3) Bubble up non-retryable errors to user with a clear code and remediation link.

- Observability: add token-level tracing (trace_id propagated from request -> model -> tool calls) and log structured events for each tool invocation (latency, outcome, error_code).

Suggested next steps for pairing session agenda (20/25/45 min breakdown):
- 20m: SDK auth flow + sample repo walkthrough (Ben)
- 25m: Live wiring of fx_read + reranker + submitPaymentProposal (Karthik)
- 45m: Q&A and mapping of OptiCore's error codes to Redwood recommended mapping (all)

I'll follow up with a short gist we can paste into the pairing session for quick copy/paste.

-Karthik
